The correct fix is ISS-2986 stamping the sentinel, not curmudgeon self-suppressing repeat audits by grep-recognition.

deeper_analysis: The dispatcher-state artifact (curmudgeon-dispatcher-state.json) generated at 2026-07-16T01:06:12Z lists chg-20260712-0010-003 as the sole unaudited critical/strategic change file within 7d. This is factually inconsistent with the reviews record: three REACTIVE-AUDIT files (07-13, 07-14, 07-15) each cite this exact change_file as their audit_scope. The dispatcher script (compute-curmudgeon-dispatcher-state.js:254) filters by change.audited_at not by the presence of a downstream REACTIVE-AUDIT review. Nothing in the pipeline writes change.audited_at (grep -rn audited_at monitor/prompts monitor/scripts returns only the reader). ISS-2986 (opened 2026-07-15T02:12:19Z, assigned-tinker) already captures this gap and is the correct place to land the fix; duplicating the finding here would be low-value churn. Todays audit is therefore consolidation-only. Coverage of the underlying change is complete: (a) mechanical fix landed via EXP-666 + ISS-2973 closure; (b) narrative-judgment follow-up in flight via ISS-2985 + EXP-669; (c) infra fix in flight via ISS-2986. No new ISS or EXP is needed. The dispatcher will re-fire this branch on 2026-07-17 + 07-18 unless the tinker fix ships; if it does, todays file demonstrates the expected steady-state behavior after a change is audited (short consolidation, defer to in-flight work items).
